expectations.text: Report identifies that the plan specifies rate limiting by IP address but the code uses session IDs
expectations.evidence: Report states under 'Deviations from Plan (Critical Semantic Mismatch)': 'The implementation tracks session_id instead of ip_address throughout. The plan specifies IP-based rate limiting — every method signature in the plan uses ip_address as the parameter name and as the conceptual key.'

expectations.text: Report notes that method signatures use session_id parameter where the plan specifies ip_address
expectations.evidence: Report lists all mismatches: 'Plan: check_rate_limit(ip_address) → Implementation: check_rate_limit(session_id)', 'Plan: record_request(ip_address) → Implementation: record_request(session_id)', etc.

expectations.text: Report flags that check_rate_limit, record_request, and get_remaining all accept session_id instead of ip_address
expectations.evidence: Report explicitly lists: 'Plan: check_rate_limit(ip_address) → Implementation: check_rate_limit(session_id)', 'Plan: record_request(ip_address) → Implementation: record_request(session_id)', 'Plan: get_remaining(ip_address) → Implementation: get_remaining(session_id)'.

expectations.text: Report flags that allowlist operations use session_id instead of ip_address
expectations.evidence: Report lists: 'Plan: is_allowlisted(ip_address) → Implementation: is_allowlisted(session_id)', 'Plan: add_to_allowlist(ip_address) → Implementation: add_to_allowlist(session_id)', 'Plan: remove_from_allowlist(ip_address) → Implementation: remove_from_allowlist(session_id)'.

expectations.text: Report confirms all tests pass despite the semantic mismatch
expectations.evidence: Report shows 'All 8 tests pass' with all listed as PASSED, and states: 'The implementation is functionally correct for a generic identifier-based rate limiter and all 8 automated tests pass.'

expectations.text: Report does NOT simply claim the plan is fully implemented just because tests pass
expectations.evidence: Report explicitly states: 'there is a critical semantic mismatch: the plan specifies IP-based rate limiting but the code uses session IDs as the limiting key. The security goal of the plan (blocking abusive IPs) is not realized.'

expectations.text: Report identifies that get_top_offenders returns session IDs not IP addresses as the plan requires
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Plan: get_top_offenders(n) returns "IP addresses" → Implementation returns session_id values'.

expectations.text: Report classifies this as a semantic deviation, not just a naming difference — the tracking dimension (IP vs session) changes the security behavior
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Wrong abstraction level: Session IDs and IP addresses are fundamentally different concepts. An IP may have multiple sessions; rate limiting by session is a weaker protection against abuse from a single IP. The original security goal (protecting against IP-based abuse) is not achieved.'

claims.evidence: Report states: 'api_gateway.py contains a dead method _get_session_id(request_context) (line 13–14) that is never called by any other method.'

claims.claim: Tests use sess-XXX style identifiers rather than IP addresses
claims.evidence: Report states: 'The tests also use sess-XXX style identifiers (e.g., "sess-001", "sess-heavy") rather than IP addresses (e.g., "192.168.1.1"), so the test suite validates the wrong semantic domain.'

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions, evals look solid. The assertions correctly test whether the report identifies the IP vs session-ID distinction as a semantic issue with security implications, not merely a naming preference.
